Thus a permanently failing retrieval yields an infinite reload loop with only 'Loading Discussion...' and no error state — a real behavioral defect (no failure path) introduced by this new feature.

judged_text: The loading page reloads every 30 seconds forever with no terminal state or error signal when retrieval never produces a topic. When fetch_http bails silently (embed_by_username blank, readability returns nothing, the remote URL 404s), TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed stays nil on every reload and the embedding page shows 'Loading Discussion...' indefinitely, with the client polling the server forever — the async chain has no failure representation at the consumer boundary.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces an embed loading flow that can loop indefinitely with no terminal/error state: when `EmbedController#best` can’t find a topic (`TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed` nil) it enqueues `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` and renders `embed/loading` (new). That loading view unconditionally reloads the page every 30s (`setTimeout(... document.location.reload(), 30000)`). On the backend, `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` can silently no-op when the configured user is missing (`return if user.blank?`), and `perform_retrieve` can exit without creating an embed if prerequisites aren’t met (e.g., no user). Nothing in the controller/view surfaces failure, so the client will keep polling forever if retrieval never results in a `TopicEmbed` row. This is a diff-grounded missing failure/timeout representation rather than a provable logic error.
